verdict:
ESCALATE on four independent mandatory triggers: discordant benches, an ADVANCE outcome (blue's reduced STARTER), self-reported broken verification (IBKR search_contracts permission-denied at BOTH benches, so every price-relationship claim in the record is arithmetic off a machine snapshot), and a binding dated binary at 2026-08-24. The escalation must land by 2026-08-21.

DECISIVE TAPE CORRECTION MADE AT ADJUDICATION (IBKR works now; the denial was bench-side permission, not an outage). Blue's central overturn - 'the post-print selloff fully round-tripped within six sessions; red's FLAT rests on a discount that no longer exists' - is half right and materially overstated. Verified IBKR daily closes: 8/04 36.28 | 8/05 36.10 (pre-print close - blue's $36.10 arithmetic is CONFIRMED exactly) | 8/06 33.43 (intraday low 29.86) | 8/07 33.61 | 8/10 33.75 | 8/11 34.14 | 8/12 33.26 | 8/13 35.92 | 8/14 34.78 last, -3.01% on the day. So: (a) blue's reconstruction of the pre-print close is correct and red's implicit claim that $35.92 was 'the post-print adjudicated level' is wrong on its face; but (b) the CURRENT price is $34.78, i.e. -3.7% net through the print, not -0.5%. The pack's $35.92 is the 8/13 close - a +8.0% ONE-SESSION spike off 8/12's $33.26 that gave back 3.0% the next day. Blue built its decisive finding on the single highest print of the window. Neither bench's number survives: the market's settled verdict on the print is a modest negative, not zero (blue) and not -7.5% (red).

WHAT SURVIVES BOTH BENCHES. Red kills the framing and wins it: 'nobody adjudicated this' is dead (the 8/6 reaction was a real -7.4% session on management's own cut of industry purchase originations to a low-to-mid-single-digit DECLINE, plus 500 layoffs and an FY guide of $2.92-2.96B vs street $2.98B); revenue is flat-to-decelerating, not accelerating (Q1 was also +18%; Q3 guides to ~11%); and ~72% of incremental growth comes from the litigated segment plus the just-guided-down segment. Blue wins on three corrections: the $10.24-style aggregation error does not apply here but the buyback one does - Q2's decelerated $200M pace still annualizes to ~9.9% of an ~$8.1B cap, so the thesis's '~10% annualized' survives at the SLOWER pace and red's 'overstates 2x' attacks a claim the thesis never made; the Q1 PR's third-party Comscore datum (127M unique visitors, +12% YoY) contradicts red's 'ARPU on a shrinking audience'; and the flush zone blue wants to buy ($31.65-33.23) demonstrably printed.

WHY THIS IS NOT ADVANCE-BY-DRAFT. Doctrine: valuation -> price gate ONLY. Both benches agree the name is fair-not-dislocated on the honest multiple (~16.6x EV/(EBITDA-SBC) against GAAP net loss of $(4)M and deceleration to ~11%); the AI-disintermediation refutation is real but is a narrative correction, not a valuation edge. The only remaining edge is a bench trial the thesis itself labels 'not estimable' - which is an UNPRICEABLE BINARY, and the response taxonomy has no instrument that converts an unpriceable binary into a starter. Blue's own construction concedes this by cutting size rather than answering it. Additionally the dislocation doctrine is unsatisfied: no forced seller is identified anywhere in the record - the -63% drawdown is a multi-quarter de-rating plus a guide cut, which is repricing, not liquidation.

PACK/TAPE AUDIT. Pack dd52 -0.642; both benches quoted -61.7%; actual at $34.78 vs 52w high $93.88 = -62.9%. Red quoted pct_off_low +22.9%; actual vs 52w low $29.23 is +19.1%. Both benches overstated the bounce and understated the drawdown - small, but the same direction, and both derived from the stale snapshot rather than the tape.

RECOMMENDED DISPOSITION TO THE ESCALATION. Hold WATCH with the existing $29.50 gate (red explicitly supports full entry on a trial-headline flush toward the $29.23 low; blue's demonstrated fill zone was $31.65-33.23). Do NOT seat a pre-trial starter at $34.78: you would be paying ~19% above the gate for exposure to a two-week bench trial whose remedy phase runs weeks past 8/24, with no forced seller and no valuation edge. The trial is the entry generator, not the risk to be front-run. || SESSION RULING: ESCALATION RULED: KILL entry-now. The adjudicator's own tape re-pull corrected blue's decisive finding (net -3.7% not -0.5%; the pack price was a one-session spike). Remaining edge = an antitrust binary both benches concede is unpriceable — and size-cutting is NOT an instrument for unpriceability (doctrine: bounded business risk cuts size; unpriceable binaries gate). NO position into the 8/24 FTC trial; re-court POST-outcome. $29.50 gate stands as review-not-buy.
